title: The Mysterious Traveler
paragraphs: A mystery, suspense, and speculative-fiction anthology introduced by an enigmatic traveler who guides listeners into tales of crime, fate, the supernatural, and strange possibilities.

Mutual anthology of strange, terrifying, criminal, supernatural and speculative stories created by Robert A. Arthur and David Kogan. Maurice Tarplin’s recurring Mysterious Traveler frames the stories with a train-journey motif. The frozen GRH snapshot contains 70 surviving/archive objects from a much larger original run.
GRH documents the program through Mutual anthology run (December 5, 1943 to September 16, 1952) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|maurice-tarplin|Maurice Tarplin]] (performer on 65 recordings), David Kogan (writer on 60 recordings, director on 51 recordings, and producer on 50 recordings), Robert A. Arthur (writer on 60 recordings, director on 30 recordings, and producer on 29 recordings), Carl Caruso (announcer on 15 recordings), Paul Taubman (organist on 11 recordings), Al Fanelli (organist on 10 recordings), and Jock MacGregor (director on 10 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.50630574777d6937|Don Lee Network]] (broadcast on network), and [[org|org.5503c31f28e9e966|KXOA]] (aircheck from station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include murder, homicide and criminal violence, ghosts, curses and supernatural return, speculative science, inventions and experiments, dreams, obsession, fear and psychological instability, war, Hitler and wartime catastrophe, and space, rockets and other worlds.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Wartime fear and enemy imagery, Postwar science and technological anxiety, Low-cost sustaining network anthology, and Mysterious Traveler cross-media franchise.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] (42 shared credited people), [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (41 shared credited people), [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]] (38 shared credited people), [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]] (38 shared credited people), and [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (36 shared credited people).
